newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat falls to new lows on harvest prospects.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat falls to new lows on harvest prospects.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed sharply lower and notched new lows on prospects for a resumption soon of active harvesting of the U.S. winter wheat crop, traders said.
"The harvest is opening up today and in most places for the weekend plus corn isn't helping out wheat either," said Dan Cekander, analyst with FIMAT Futures.

New-crop July set a new contract low of $3.25 a bushel, below the previous low of $3.28 set Monday. The $3.25 level is also a new three-year low and is the lowest level for a nearby contract since $3.03-1/2 was hit in July 1994.

Showers this week slowed combining of the Kansas wheat crop but there are signs harvesting soon will be back to full speed amid hot and drier weather. The soft red winter harvest also is gaining speed in the southernmost reaches of the SRW Belt. Better-than-expected crop yields have consistently been reported in the HRW and SRW combining areas.
During the waning 15 minutes of trade, Rosenthal Collins sold six million bushels of September and was offering more, traders said.
Wheat closed three to 7-1/4 cents lower, with July down 7-1/4 at $3.25-3/4 and September down 7 at $3.36.
Kansas City trade sources said harvest may resume as early as Friday afternoon and said the only rainfall overnight was in eastern Kansas, a minimal wheat producing region.
Position squaring was featured because USDA Monday is slated to release its updated stocks report and acreage report plus Monday is first notice day for deliveries on the CBOT July contracts.
There were ideas for wheat deliveries to be heavy from one million to three million bushels, the traders said.
Traders said the market shrugged off perceptions of bullish export activity including news overnight Tunisia bought 150,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat and news Taiwan bought 66,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat.

In addition to the aggressive late selling by Rosenthal Collins, on the day FIMAT Futures sold 1.5 million bushels of September, and Smith Barney and Tenco Inc each sold one million September, traders said.

In spread trading, Smith Barney did 2.5 million bushels of July/September at 9-1/2 to 9-3/4 cents premium September, Refco Inc did one million July/September at 9-1/2 cents premium September and Smith Barney spread one million September/July at 9-1/2 cents, premium September, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 27,000 contracts, above the 25,827 traded Thursday.

In wheat options, Prudential Securities bought 200 September $3.60 calls at 5-3/4 cents, Rosenthal Collins bought 100 September $3.60 calls at six cents and Prudential Securities bought 100 September $3.50 calls at nine cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,700 contracts, above the 4,530 traded Thursday.
